# Convert AVI to MP4

- Route: `/tools/convert-avi-to-mp4`
- Kind: `tool`
- Category: `video`
- Slug: `convert-avi-to-mp4`

## Summary

Modernize old .avi videos into a compact MP4 that plays on every phone, browser, and TV. (Video tools)

## Details

AVI is a classic Windows container from the DivX/Xvid era. The files are often large and use codecs that modern phones, browsers, and TVs no longer play. Converting AVI to MP4 re-encodes the video to efficient H.264 and the audio to AAC, producing a smaller file that plays on anything you own today.
### What it does
- Converts legacy .avi (Xvid, DivX, MJPEG, and more) to MP4.
- Locks the output to MP4 (H.264 + AAC) for modern playback.
- Usually produces a noticeably smaller file than the AVI source.
- An old AVI can be cut down and scaled while it is converted.
### How to use it
1. Upload your AVI: Drop in an old .avi file from an archive or camera.
2. Output is locked to MP4: MP4 is preset — nothing to configure.
3. Convert: We re-encode to H.264 + AAC.
4. Download: Save a smaller, modern MP4.
### Supported formats
- Input: avi
- Output: mp4
- Output is locked to MP4 (H.264 + AAC, yuv420p, +faststart).
### Technical details
- AVI commonly uses Xvid/DivX (MPEG-4 Part 2); H.264 is roughly twice as efficient, so the MP4 is usually much smaller.
- We force yuv420p so the result plays in browsers and on social platforms.
- Interlaced AVI captures may benefit from the deinterlace option in the full video converter.
### Use cases
- Old video archives: Modernize camcorder or DVD-rip AVIs into MP4.
- Free up space: Shrink a large AVI into a smaller MP4.
- Phone & TV playback: Make an AVI play on devices that dropped AVI support.
- Upload to the web: Turn an AVI into an MP4 a site will accept.
### FAQ
Q: How do I convert AVI to MP4?
A: Upload your .avi file and click convert — the output is already set to MP4.
Q: Will the MP4 be smaller than the AVI?
A: Usually yes. H.264 is far more efficient than the Xvid/DivX codecs most AVIs use.
Q: Does it support old DivX/Xvid AVIs?
A: Yes — FFmpeg decodes the common AVI codecs and re-encodes them to H.264.
Q: Will I lose quality?
A: Re-encoding is lossy, but at High quality the difference is minimal and the file is still smaller.
